summary: Adds tenant-owned application catalogue, request, activation, configuration-link, and audit contracts while keeping deployment installation under platform control.
userImpact: Tenant administrators can view compatible installed applications and manage activation only for their current tenant.
Ordinary tenant members can use active applications but cannot activate, deactivate, approve, or configure them.
Existing platform plugin installation and settings routes remain available and retain deployment-wide authority.

instructions: Run the normal database migrations before enabling tenant marketplace routes.
Existing deployment-scoped plugins and single-tenant installations continue without tenant marketplace configuration.

configuration: Adds an opt-in deployment policy for tenant activation requests; direct tenant-admin activation remains the compatibility default.
Plugin manifests may expose safe catalogue metadata, a configuration schema reference, and a plugin-owned tenant configuration link without registry or infrastructure data.

changes: Adds tenant.apps.read, tenant.apps.request, tenant.apps.manage, and tenant.apps.use authorization actions.
Adds tenant-safe catalogue, application detail, activation/deactivation, activation-request, approval, configuration-link, and activation-audit APIs.
Retains the existing tenant enablement endpoint as a backward-compatible alias governed by tenant application actions.

notes: The migration expands tenant plugin enablement with lifecycle status, optimistic revision, activation request state, and safe configuration projections.
Rollback removes only tenant marketplace state after affected tenant applications have been deactivated.

security: Every tenant marketplace query and mutation derives tenant identity from authenticated request context and never accepts a tenant ID in the body.
Catalogue responses exclude pricing, registry credentials, infrastructure topology, raw entitlement documents, and sibling-tenant state.
Activation mutations require optimistic revision, idempotency, tenant application permissions, and tenant-scoped audit.
documentation: Documents marketplace ownership, tenant actions, lifecycle state transitions, compatibility aliases, safe catalogue projection, and rollback.
knownLimitations: Signed tenant eligibility projection and runtime/asynchronous reconciliation are delivered by the next dependency-ordered slice.
rollback: Deactivate tenant applications and wait for lifecycle operations to settle before rolling back the migration.
Continue using the existing platform plugin routes and deployment-scoped enablement after rollback.
validation: Tests cover tenant-admin activation, member use-only access, platform installation separation, idempotency, optimistic revision conflicts, sibling-tenant denial, secret-free safe projections, and existing route compatibility.
The pooled reference-plugin lane activates different tenants independently and proves deactivation does not affect a sibling tenant.
